chapter: Chez Florence, the Hot Club and Django
title: Django's ear and his two-finger technique
summary: Briggs calls Django another Bechet with a wonderful ear who learned tunes by following chords, playing with two fingers while using the paralysed ones to bar.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Well, how did he -- I mean he didn't know any music. I mean, he just felt his way along; is that right?
He was another Bechet. He had a wonderful ear. His ear was trained, and you'd hit a chord, and he's got it.
In other words, he'd just follow the tune right along, and learn it.
Oh, he was terrific. Have you ever seen him? He plays with two fingers, you know.
Yeh, I knew that. And he had -- Grapelly told me that he would -- sometimes he would lift those other two paralyzed fingers up onto the frets --
And he'd sort of bar with them.
Yes, oh, yes, he'd bar with them.
